questions.question: Explain the advantages and disadvantages of a bonus issue.
questions.solution_html:
• Advantages of bonus issue
  • a) The company does not need to pay cash.
  • b) Increases Share Liquidity
  • c) Indicates strong financial position and accumulated profits
  • d) Rewards Shareholders
  • e) Better Capital Structure
  • Disadvantages
  • a) No Real Wealth Increase
  • b) Earnings Per Share (EPS) Falls
  • c) No Cash Benefit to Shareholders
  • d) Future Dividend Burden
  • e) Lead to speculative Trading in stock market
questions.final_answer: Option The company does not need to pay cash.

questions.question: Explain with example each the following / a. Long term borrowings and short-term borrowings b Provisions and short-term provisions c. Trade payables and trade receivables
questions.solution_html:
• Long-term borrowings And Short-term borrowings
  • Long-term Borrowings are loans or debts that are repayable after more than 12 months .
  • They are shown under non-current liabilities in the Balance Sheet. Short-term Borrowings are
  • loans that must be repaid within 12 months. They are shown under current liabilities.
  • Provisions and short term provisions: These are liabilities of uncertain amount or timing. They
  • are created to cover expected future expenses or losses. Can be long-term or short- term
  • depending on when they are expected to be settled.
  • Trade Payables vs Trade Receivables
  • Trade Payables: Amounts a business owes to suppliers for goods or services purchased on credit. It
  • is a liability and includes Creditors and Bills Payables
  • Trade Receivables : Amounts owed to the business by customers for goods or services sold on
  • credit. It is an asset and includes Debtors and Bills receivables.
questions.final_answer: credit. It is an asset and includes Debtors and Bills receivables

questions.question: Explain the advantages and disadvantages of a bonus issue.
questions.solution_html:
• Advantages of bonus issue
  • a) The company does not need to pay cash.
  • b) Increases Share Liquidity
  • c) Indicates strong financial position and accumulated profits
  • d) Rewards Shareholders
  • e) Better Capital Structure
  • Disadvantages
  • a) No Real Wealth Increase
  • b) Earnings Per Share (EPS) Falls
  • c) No Cash Benefit to Shareholders
  • d) Future Dividend Burden
  • e) Lead to speculative Trading in stock market
questions.final_answer: Option The company does not need to pay cash.

questions.question: Explain with example each the following / a. Long term borrowings and short-term borrowings b Provisions and short-term provisions c. Trade payables and trade receivables
questions.solution_html:
• Long-term borrowings And Short-term borrowings
  • Long-term Borrowings are loans or debts that are repayable after more than 12 months .
  • They are shown under non-current liabilities in the Balance Sheet. Short-term Borrowings are
  • loans that must be repaid within 12 months. They are shown under current liabilities.
  • Provisions and short term provisions: These are liabilities of uncertain amount or timing. They
  • are created to cover expected future expenses or losses. Can be long-term or short- term
  • depending on when they are expected to be settled.
  • Trade Payables vs Trade Receivables
  • Trade Payables: Amounts a business owes to suppliers for goods or services purchased on credit. It
  • is a liability and includes Creditors and Bills Payables
  • Trade Receivables : Amounts owed to the business by customers for goods or services sold on
  • credit. It is an asset and includes Debtors and Bills receivables.
questions.final_answer: credit. It is an asset and includes Debtors and Bills receivables
